chunks: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'For Paradise there is a gate called the Gate of the Mujahideen. They will proceed toward it and it shall be open, and they will be girded with their swords, while the multitude stand at the place of gathering and the angels welcome them.'

Then he said: 'So whoever abandons jihad, God, Mighty and Majestic, will clothe him with humiliation and poverty in his livelihood and obliterate his religion. Verily, God, Mighty and Majestic, has made my community self-sufficient by the hooves of its cavalry and the points of its spears.'

key_terms.الجهاد: Jihad — striving/struggle in God's cause, encompassing both defensive warfare and broader effort for justice
key_terms.الْمَوْقِف: Al-Mawqif — the station of gathering on the Day of Resurrection
key_terms.بَابُ الْمُجَاهِدِينَ: Gate of the Mujahideen — a specific gate of Paradise reserved for those who fought in God's cause
key_terms.ذُلّ: Dhull — humiliation, degradation; used here as spiritual and worldly consequence of abandoning duty
key_terms.سَنَابِك: Sanabik — hooves (plural of sunbuk); metaphor for military strength and cavalry
key_terms.مَرَاكِز: Marakiz — points/tips; here referring to the tips of spears, symbolizing military power

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about the Gate of the Mujahideen in Paradise?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through Imam al-Sadiq (AS) from the Prophet (SAWW), describes the honor awaiting those who engage in jihad: a special gate of Paradise dedicated to the Mujahideen, where they enter girded with swords while angels welcome them at the Day of Resurrection. The Prophet then warns that those who abandon jihad will be punished with humiliation, poverty, and a weakening of their faith. The final statement reflects a key principle in early Islamic governance: the community's dignity and sufficiency depend on its military preparedness and willingness to defend itself. The original audience would have understood this as a direct call to arms for the defense of the nascent Muslim community against external threats.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘For the Paradise there is a door called ‘Al-Mujahideen’ (The Combatants). They would be going to it, so it be open and they would be collared with their swords, and the troops would be in the Pausing Station, and the Angels would be welcoming them’.

Then he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘So the one who neglects the Jihad, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic would Clothe him with disgrace and poverty in his living, and Obliterate (remove) his Religion. May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Make my<sup>saww</sup> community to be self-sufficient by the hooves of its cavalry horses and the points of its spears’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father, from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah has said, ‘In paradise there is a door which is called ‘the door of people serving in the army’. They walk to it and it is open and they have their swords fixed on them ready and in place. The angels welcome them.’

He then said, ‘Whoever ignores joining the army, Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, dresses him up with humiliation, poverty and his religion is destroyed. Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, makes my followers self-sufficient through the hooves of their horses and the points of their spears.’”
